newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong issues draft of banking practice code.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong issues draft of banking practice code.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the defacto central bank, on Friday issued a draft Code of Banking Practice for public consultation.

"The introduction of such a code will help promote good banking practices and a fair and transparent relationship between authorised institutions and their customers," HKMA executive director (banking policy) Raymond Li said.
"It should be noted that the standards being proposed are in line with that of other financial centres," Li told reporters.
The code covers the relationship between banks and customers, opening and operation of accounts and loans, card services, payment services and debt collection.
The final version is expected to be issued in the first half of this year after a consultation period ending February 28.
Banking institutions were expected to observe the code although it was non-statutory, Li said.
"It's actually in the interest of the institutions to follow this code," he said, adding banks that did not abide by it would be less competitive by those who did.
The HKMA would monitor compliance with the code, but how it would handle violations depended on each case, Li said.
"I think the bulk of the banking sector comply with most of the code already," he noted.
